headline: High risk of filesystem conflict and medium prompt-injection/data-leakage exposure; no direct evidence of a documented pairwise bridge.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Mentat reads files from the filesystem and applies diff-based edits, while the course agent also reads/writes files and processes papers, metadata, and secrets. A shared filesystem bridge is explicitly present in Mentat’s concurrency model, so attacker-controlled content in shared files could influence either agent. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace directory
IF either agent consumes file contents as trusted instructions or prompts
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Mark shared inputs read-only for one agent
Add a manual review step before applying file-derived instructions
Use provenance labels on files exchanged between agents
requires-engineering: add sandboxed provenance filtering

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents read and write files, and both handle sensitive material: Mentat handles model-provider API keys, while the course agent handles configuration secrets and research data. Because Mentat shares state via filesystem and the course agent’s files include .env.example and notebooks, a shared workspace could expose secrets or papers across agents. No direct isolation mechanism is documented.
conditions: IF the two agents share a writable directory
IF secrets or papers are stored in files accessible to both agents
mitigations: Use separate directories for secrets and working files
Exclude .env and secret-bearing files from shared mounts
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately after a shared run
Restrict one agent to read-only access on sensitive folders
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem ACLs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Mentat can modify git state and write the filesystem; the course agent can execute shell commands, install packages, spawn subprocesses, and also write the filesystem. In a shared directory, both can mutate the same working tree without any locking or coordination primitive being documented, creating a strong conflict risk and possible irreversible repo corruption.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same git checkout
IF either agent writes concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Run agents in separate clones
Serialize write access with a manual lock file
Disable git-mutating actions for one agent during overlap
Take a backup branch before concurrent work
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Mentat produces diff-based edit proposals, and the course agent’s API surface includes agentic ask/stream endpoints that can consume generated content. If the course agent treats Mentat’s output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or content generation. The pathway is plausible but not directly evidenced, so uncertainty is resolved upward from low to medium.
conditions: IF the course agent ingests Mentat-generated diffs or summaries without verification
IF downstream automation uses that output to produce user-facing content or actions
mitigations: Require human review of Mentat diffs before reuse
Add a verification checklist for any imported edits
Keep generated summaries separate from executable instructions
Log source attribution for reused outputs
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Mentat is documented as handling model-provider API keys, while the course agent handles configuration secrets and research data. If both are run in one environment, retention or logging differences could expose secrets or academic data beyond intended scope. The profiles do not show a residency mismatch, so the risk is compliance-policy mismatch rather than a higher-severity jurisdiction issue.
conditions: IF shared logs retain prompts, files, or secrets beyond the intended retention window
IF the same operator account accesses both agents’ sensitive data
mitigations: Disable verbose logging for secret-bearing sessions
Purge temporary files after each run
Store secrets outside shared project directories
Document retention rules for both workflows
requires-engineering: align retention and access-control policies
